reply_text:
I found two dated predictions from 2015. Both are about Tesla's self-driving cars, not general AI, and I saw both only in news articles, not in a transcript or anything Musk wrote himself.

- **14 October 2015, Autopilot press call.** Asked when Tesla would have a car with full "Level 4" autonomy, Musk said: "From a technology standpoint, Tesla will have a car that can do full autonomy in about three years, maybe a bit sooner." Green Car Reports quotes him in its 16 October article, which says the call was on "Wednesday afternoon". I worked out the 14 October date from that, so check it.
- **21 December 2015, Fortune.** "We're going to end up with complete autonomy, and I think we will have complete autonomy in approximately two years." The article says he spoke to Fortune on his commute.

I counted these because self-driving is an AI capability with a date attached. If your rules mean general AI only, both drop out and 2015 has no candidates.

Other things I checked that don't qualify:
- **Nvidia conference, March 2015:** "we'll be there in a few years" has no date and isn't about general AI.
- **Boao Forum, March 2015:** He said superintelligence would be "superhuman almost immediately". That's about how fast it would take off, not when it arrives.
- **OpenAI launch interview with Steven Levy, December 2015:** No timeline from Musk.
- **LessWrong post "Musk on AGI Timeframes":** It seems to cover his late-2014 "five year timeframe" comment, but I didn't open it.

I ran all 10 searches and used all 6 page openings. The Fortune and Wikipedia pages loaded fine even though my code first flagged them as errors.
